definitions.explanation: Engineering and policy efforts to control rivers and floodwaters — including dams, levees, channel improvements, and watershed management — so that flooding is reduced and water resources are usable.

examples.japanese: {治水|ちすい}{工事|こうじ}が{進|すす}んでいる。
{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}には{多|おお}くの{治水|ちすい}{事業|じぎょう}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: Many flood-control projects were carried out during the Edo period.

examples.japanese: ダムは{治水|ちすい}と{利水|りすい}の{両方|りょうほう}の{役割|やくわり}を{果|は}たしている。
examples.english: Dams serve both flood-control and water-utilization roles.

examples.japanese: {近年|きんねん}の{豪雨|ごうう}の{頻発|ひんぱつ}を{受|う}け、{自治体|じちたい}は{治水|ちすい}{対策|たいさく}を{強化|きょうか}している。
examples.english: In response to the recent frequency of torrential rains, local governments are strengthening flood-control measures.

notes:
{治水|ちすい} literally combines {治|ち} (to govern, to manage) and {水|すい} (water). It refers to flood control and the broader management of rivers and water flow — historically a core responsibility of governments in flood-prone Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {治水|ちすい}{事業|じぎょう}: flood-control / river-management project
- {治水|ちすい}{工事|こうじ}: flood-control construction
- {治水|ちすい}{対策|たいさく}: flood-control measures
- {治水|ちすい}ダム: flood-control dam
- {治水|ちすい}{計画|けいかく}: flood-control plan
- {治水|ちすい}と{利水|りすい}: flood control and water utilization (a stock pairing)

VERB USAGE:
- As a する verb: {治水|ちすい}する is technically possible but rare; the noun-form usages above are far more common.

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- {利水|りすい}: water utilization (irrigation, water supply, hydroelectric — the complement to {治水|ちすい})
- {防災|ぼうさい}: disaster prevention (broader category)
- {堤防|ていぼう}: levee, embankment
- ダム: dam
- {放水路|ほうすいろ}: floodway, drainage channel

CULTURAL / HISTORICAL NOTE:
Flood control has been a major civil-engineering theme in Japan due to typhoons and steep rivers. Famous historical {治水|ちすい} efforts include the {木曽川|きそがわ} treaty works overseen by Satsuma engineers in the Edo period and the modern {利根川|とねがわ} flood-control system around the Kanto region.
